text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Diagnosis: a structured headache history, a red-flag screen (SNNOOP10) at every visit, a 14-day headache diary of attacks, features, triggers and medicine days, and ICHD-3 criteria; no neuroimaging for a stable long-standing pattern without red flags, with clear reasons that would change that
  • Neurology (headache medicine) consultation to confirm the diagnosis and advise on acute and preventive treatment
  • Acute treatment at intake: naproxen early in an attack, with metoclopramide for nausea, no more than two days a week; stop the over-the-counter combination analgesic with caffeine; no opioids or butalbital
  • Acute treatment after the diagnosis: sumatriptan 100 mg with naproxen early in a migraine attack, a second sumatriptan dose after two hours if needed; a gepant or lasmiditan if a triptan fails or becomes unsuitable
  • Medication overuse headache prevention: acute-medicine days counted in the diary, with limits of fewer than 10 days a month for a triptan or combination analgesic and fewer than 15 for an NSAID; never caffeine pills or combination products
  • Preventive treatment, since bouts bring six or more migraine days a month with severe disability: propranolol extended-release, starting at 80 mg and raised to 120 mg if tolerated, with pulse, blood pressure, energy and mood checked; efficacy judged at two to three months (at least half as many migraine days); a CGRP monoclonal antibody as the next option, or sooner if propranolol is not tolerated; topiramate and amitriptyline not chosen because of their effects on concentration and morning alertness
  • Lifestyle and triggers: a fixed wake and sleep time, regular meals on working days, a steady modest amount of caffeine, fluids, daily walks, and a stress plan for long working days with breaks from reading; relaxation training and biofeedback offered
  • Wrist and writing: an occupational therapy visit for hand function, a wrist splint for long writing sessions, dictation software, and a desk set up to spare the wrist and neck

resource.title: Thomas Jefferson synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recurrent disabling headache in a working statesman: a 47-year-old cabinet secretary, seven weeks into a demanding new post, comes in a week into a bout of the headaches he has had since his twenties. The episode covers a structured headache history with a red-flag screen and no neuroimaging when none is indicated, a headache diary that confirms ICHD-3 migraine without aura, disability measured with the MIDAS, acute treatment with an NSAID and a triptan and the place of gepants and lasmiditan, why opioids and butalbital are avoided, counting acute-medicine days to prevent medication overuse headache, the criteria for preventive treatment and the choice among propranolol, topiramate, amitriptyline and a CGRP monoclonal antibody under the 2021 American Headache Society consensus, its 2024 position statement and the 2025 ACP guidelines, sleep, meals, caffeine and work stress as triggers, and an old badly healed wrist injury that makes writing slow and painful.
